Real-template fixtures, task t_ce1fd4c0

Captured on PC4070TI using llama.cpp 6c5afc86ae84448ae4d744e357017e2c490ad9c3.
backend-A.json preserves the integral /apply-template requests/responses for text
and tools, plus /tokenize IDs for the tools prompt. No generated output is in
this fixture: qualification stopped before inference.
A.jinja and B.jinja are extracted verbatim from the existing Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf
and granite-4.2-3b-Q4_K_M.gguf metadata respectively, not rewritten templates.

Baseline 647295c (0.3.34) and candidate e07777a have identical chattemplate.py
SHA256 615a53eb810b42cdef2a24ecc097faac4be36de4638afab7481ea4b88e755459.
Both strip the OpenAI wrapper, rendering 4948 characters / 1905 IDs for tools;
the real backend preserves it, rendering 4982 characters / 1915 IDs.
The explicit openai opt-in reproduces the latter byte-for-byte. The strata
default and existing issue95 golden remain unchanged. B is self-unwrapping;
its fixture is not a substitute for real backend qualification.

Tokenizer files remain outside the source tree. The task's offline verifier
uses the official pinned tokenizer files checked against all GGUF vocab IDs
and merges. The full impact/RED/byte/ID records live in the task workspace.

library-variants.json is captured from the exact existing common chat shared
library at 6c5afc86, invoked via a small C++ adapter with model=nullptr. No model,
backend or generation is initialized. Both integral base prompts were first
matched byte-for-byte against the real server captures above. Twenty variants
cover order, strict extras, absent description, two tools, compact arguments,
Unicode, empty assistants, developer/intermediate system roles and text parts.
The initial opt-in failed eleven variants; only the opt-in branch was corrected.
Default Strata and all four already successful real-generation prompts remain
byte/ID identical. Capability supports_object_arguments is true for both real
templates, so the common library parses argument strings before rendering.
